overlaps.paper_title: Diminishing Returns Epistasis Among Beneficial Mutations Decelerates Adaptation
overlaps.paper_value: Per-allele relative-effect trend; no printed DRI/ICI scalar or coefficient
overlaps.locator: Fig. 1 caption, printed p.1190; Results, printed p.1191
overlaps.definition_quote: “Variation in relative selective effect (normalized to maximum s_i) of each allele as a function of the fitness of the background it was introduced into”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper presents a relative effect-versus-background relationship for each evolved allele. GraphFLA computes one Pearson correlation across node fitness and node-mean improving-edge gains.
overlaps.reason: No reproduction was attempted. The paper reports allele-specific relative effects/trends, not the GraphFLA node-averaged landscape correlation.

overlaps.paper_title: Negative Epistasis Between Beneficial Mutations in an Evolving Bacterial Population
overlaps.locator: Fig. 4, printed p.1195; Results, printed pp.1194–1195
overlaps.definition_quote: “Each panel includes the Pearson correlation coefficient and its significance.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Khan et al. report one Pearson r per focal mutation over its mutation-specific background pairs. GraphFLA correlates node fitness with each node’s average over improving mutations.
overlaps.reason: The paper's coefficients are per mutation; they are not one landscape-wide Pearson coefficient across node means.

other_printed_statistic.description: Correlation between expected genotype fitness and epistatic deviation; different response from Fig. 4 mutation effect versus background fitness.
other_printed_statistic.quote: “absolute epistasis: correlation coefficient (r)=−0.578; relative epistasis: r=−0.586”

overlaps.paper_title: Global epistasis makes adaptation predictable despite sequence-level stochasticity
overlaps.paper_value: Negative trend for three targeted knockouts; no printed coefficient
overlaps.locator: Fig. 3, printed p.1521; Results, printed p.1521
overlaps.definition_quote: “The fitness effect of knocking out genes gat2, whi2, and sfl1 declines with the fitness of the background strain.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The direct analysis is three selected knockouts measured across a set of yeast backgrounds. No correlation type or numerical slope is reported; GraphFLA pools all improving mutations by node.
overlaps.reason: The paper describes selected mutation-specific trends; it does not supply a scalar target matching GraphFLA's node-mean summary.

overlaps.paper_title: Long-Term Dynamics of Adaptation in Asexual Populations
overlaps.definition_quote: “The value of g estimated for the six populations that retained the low ancestral mutation rate throughout 50,000 generations is 6.0 (95% confidence interval 5.3–6.9).”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Wiser et al. fit a population-level adaptation model with parameter g. They do not correlate observed mutation gains with background genotypes or report a local landscape index.
overlaps.reason: The printed scalar g is a trajectory-model parameter, not a correlation or slope over GraphFLA mutation edges.

other_printed_statistic.description: Correlations between grand-mean observed fitness and fitted model trajectories; not local mutation-effect/background correlations.
other_printed_statistic.quote: “the correlation coefficients for the grand means and model trajectories are 0.969 and 0.986 for the hyperbolic and power-law models, respectively”

overlaps.paper_title: Higher-fitness yeast genotypes are less robust to deleterious mutations
overlaps.locator: Fig. 2 caption, printed p.491–492; Fig. 4 caption, printed p.493; Results, printed p.492
overlaps.quote: Fig. 2: “P = 0.03, two-sided t test”; “P = 4.13 × 10−31, P = 7.83 × 10−14, P = 4.08 × 10−12, respectively, two-sided t test.” Results: “the most frequent pattern (48 cases)”; “This negative correlation is not universal; six mutations exhibit the opposite pattern.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “Histogram of regression slopes between fitness effect and background fitness for each mutation.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Johnson et al. report per-insertion slopes and DFE shifts across segregants. GraphFLA does not return the per-mutation slopes or the DFE statistics; it correlates node fitness with mean reverse-edge gains.
overlaps.reason: The paper reports per-mutation regressions and DFE statistics, not one node-aggregated landscape coefficient.

overlaps.paper_title: Global epistasis emerges from a generic model of a complex trait
overlaps.paper_value: Per-mutation/locus slope coefficient c_i; no printed pooled DRI value
overlaps.locator: Eq. 1 and accompanying text, printed p.2; Fig. 1 caption, printed p.2
overlaps.quote: “c_i quantifies the magnitude of global epistasis for locus i”; Fig. 1 caption: “the mean over 91 mutations (in red) and 5 of the 91 mutations.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Reddy & Desai define a per-locus linear slope, while GraphFLA's default is a Pearson correlation of node fitness with node-mean improving-edge gain.
overlaps.reason: The paper's c_i is mutation/locus-specific and is not one landscape-level GraphFLA-style scalar.

overlaps.paper_title: Global epistasis emerges from a generic model of a complex trait
overlaps.paper_value: Per-mutation/locus slope coefficient c_i; no printed pooled ICI value
overlaps.locator: Eq. 1 and accompanying text, printed p.2; Fig. 1 caption, printed p.2
overlaps.quote: “c_i quantifies the magnitude of global epistasis for locus i”; Fig. 1 caption: “the mean over 91 mutations (in red) and 5 of the 91 mutations.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “applies independently of whether its additive effect is deleterious (increasing-costs) or beneficial (diminishing-returns).”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Theoretical increasing-cost behavior is represented by mutation-specific slopes and residuals. GraphFLA returns a node-level correlation after averaging incoming edge costs.
overlaps.reason: No single landscape-wide increasing-cost index is defined in the article.

overlaps.paper_title: Idiosyncratic epistasis leads to global fitness–correlated trends
overlaps.locator: Fig. 3 caption and Results, printed p.633
overlaps.quote: “~44% of regression slopes deviated substantially from 1”; “b = 0.76”; “b = 1.29.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “A regression slope (b) different from 1 in these plots signifies an FCT.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Bakerlee et al. estimate per-locus FCT slopes from paired genotype fitnesses and do not split all effects into beneficial-only transitions. GraphFLA pools node-mean gains.
overlaps.reason: Per-locus, environment- and ploidy-specific regression slopes are not a single node-aggregated DRI value.

overlaps.paper_title: Idiosyncratic epistasis leads to global fitness–correlated trends

paper_value.definition: FCT slopes are not classified by beneficial/deleterious mutation sets

overlaps.locator: Fig. 3 caption and Discussion, printed pp.633, 635
overlaps.quote: “~44% of regression slopes deviated substantially from 1”; “b = 1.29.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “Because the landscapes that we studied here have no natural polarization (i.e., neither allele is the assumed WT).”
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper analyzes unpolarized fitness-correlated trends rather than an edge pool restricted to deleterious mutation effects. GraphFLA ICI is a directed cost-magnitude summary grouped by target node.
overlaps.reason: Bakerlee et al.'s unpolarized FCT slopes are not a per-deleterious-transition ICI.

overlaps.paper_title: A rugged yet easily navigable fitness landscape
overlaps.definition_quote: “The fitness gain of beneficial mutations (vertical axis) decreases in genetic backgrounds with higher fitness (horizontal axis).”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Papkou et al. pool individual beneficial mutation transitions in a linear regression. GraphFLA averages each genotype's gains before correlating nodes.
overlaps.reason: The reported trend is an edge-pooled linear regression, not the node-mean correlation returned by GraphFLA.

overlaps.paper_title: Idiosyncratic epistasis creates universals in mutational effects and evolutionary trajectories

paper_value.single_mutation_r_values: distribution; empirical per-mutation coefficients are not tabulated

overlaps.locator: Methods, ‘Examining correlation between background fitness and mutational effect’; Results, Fig. 2b
overlaps.quote: “87.8% of mutations from the yeast tRNA fitness landscape show a negative correlation between fitness effect and background fitness.”
overlaps.definition_quote: “Pearson’s correlation coefficient was calculated between mutational effect on a particular trait and background trait value for each single mutation.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Lyons et al. report per-mutation correlation distributions plus pooled r, not a Pearson correlation over node-level mean gains.
overlaps.reason: The paper's DRI/ICI evidence is distributions of per-mutation Pearson coefficients; it defines no DRI/ICI index.

overlaps.paper_title: Idiosyncratic epistasis creates universals in mutational effects and evolutionary trajectories
overlaps.paper_value: Per-mutation Pearson correlation distributions are reported for beneficial and detrimental mutation classes; no ICI-specific scalar or printed numeric coefficient is reported.
overlaps.locator: Methods, ‘Examining correlation between background fitness and mutational effect’; Results, Fig. 2b
overlaps.quote: “mutations were deemed beneficial or detrimental depending on their effect on the wild-type genotype in GFP and tRNA”
overlaps.definition_quote: “Pearson’s correlation coefficient was also calculated between all mutational effects and background trait values for each landscape.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Lyons et al. report deleterious-mutation correlation distributions and pooled r, not GraphFLA's node-averaged reverse-edge cost correlation.
overlaps.reason: No DRI/ICI scalar is defined; the published analysis is per-mutation Pearson-r distributions and a pooled r.

overlaps.paper_title: Augmenting Biological Fitness Prediction Benchmarks with Landscapes Features from GraphFLA
overlaps.locator: Appendix C.3.2, printed p.36; Tables A2–A3, printed pp.47–48
overlaps.quote: Table A2 ϵDR: 0.043, −0.319; Table A3 ϵDR: 0.391
overlaps.definition_quote: “Diminishing returns is then measured by calculating the Pearson correlation coefficient between the fitness of the background genotype, f(g), and the corresponding positive selection coefficient, s(g → g′), across all such beneficial mutations.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: Huang et al. define an edge-pooled Pearson coefficient. GraphFLA instead takes one mean effect per source node and correlates across nodes. Table values are from the GraphFLA feature computations and are not independent validation.

input.preprocessing: Not applicable; literature survey only; no feature recomputation.

overlaps.reason: The published scalar precedent is edge-pooled; GraphFLA's implementation is node-averaged. No reproduction was attempted.

overlaps.paper_title: Augmenting Biological Fitness Prediction Benchmarks with Landscapes Features from GraphFLA
overlaps.locator: Appendix C.3.2, printed p.36; Table A2, printed p.47
overlaps.definition_quote: “Increasing costs epistasis is measured by calculating the Pearson correlation coefficient between the fitness of the background genotype, f(g), and the magnitude (absolute value) of the corresponding negative selection coefficient, |s(g → g′)|, across all such deleterious mutations.”
overlaps.definition_divergence: GraphFLA's reverse-edge costs have the corresponding background and sign, but they are averaged by target genotype before correlation. This changes edge weighting and the estimand.

input.preprocessing: Not applicable; literature survey only; no feature recomputation.

overlaps.reason: The paper defines an edge-pooled scalar; GraphFLA's current implementation correlates node-level mean costs.

verdict_reason: The literature mostly reports per-mutation correlations/slopes or qualitative background-fitness trends, with a few distinct scalar/model precedents. GraphFLA's functions correlate node fitness against node-averaged improving-edge gains/costs. This is a defensible non-standard landscape summary, but it is not the per-mutation convention or Huang et al.'s published edge-pooled Pearson coefficient.
